rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 is the best race so far (score 682.8). The oval finished 20/20 (mean 2.13 s). The s-bend finished 19/20. The slalom failed in all 20 runs, with progress 0.43, 1.1 line-loss events per run, and off-track as the only end condition. Across iterations, widening the sensor row has consistently raised slalom progress: 0.15 at ±0.024 m, 0.37 at ±0.032 m, and 0.43 at ±0.036 m. The gain of the trend is slowing, and the slalom still loses the tape, so the array is probably still too narrow for its sharpest reversals.

Change 1 (geometry): widen the sensor row to x = -0.044, -0.022, 0, 0.022, 0.044 at y = 0.05. Footprint stays at 12 mm to isolate the effect of spacing. Tape stays visible to about ±0.054 m of lateral offset, beyond the current ±0.048 m.

Change 2 (gains): steering signal per metre of offset falls roughly in proportion to spacing. Spacing goes from 18 mm to 22 mm (ratio 1.22), so kp rises from 2.9 to 3.5 to keep steering authority about constant. This follows the same rule that matched the 2.6 to 2.9 step. kd scales with kp to stay near the stable kd/kp ratio of about 0.37 to 0.45, so kd goes from 1.3 to 1.5. ki stays 0, weights stay -2..2, and line_loss stays last_direction.

Change 3 (speed): base_speed drops from 1.15 to 1.1 to give more time to correct on the slalom's sharp bends. The oval has about 0.9 s of margin, so it should still finish, at roughly 2.2 s.

Expected result: slalom progress rises above 0.6, with line-loss events below 1 per run and a chance of finishing. The s-bend completion rate holds at 0.9 or better. Main risk: the wider array may increase steering oscillation on the oval. I will check steering_oscillation and line_loss_events on the oval and slalom first.
